prompts.object: Photorealistic special-education card atlas EXACT FIVE EQUAL WIDTH columns and TWO EQUAL HEIGHT rows (ten square cells, canvas aspect ratio 5:2). Will be cropped at 20%,40%,60%,80% width and 50% height. EVERY object entirely visible with 15% safe margin on each tile edge, no overlap/neighbor fragments. Matching top/bottom pairs SAME color, size, orientation and object baseline. No text, numbers, symbols, borders, arrows, glow or logos. Real-life recognizable objects. Pure white clean seamless backgrounds, only very soft ground shadow below subject. Teach HARD versus SOFT through visible response to pressure, not color. TOP ROW HARD objects with one adult index finger gently pressing down from above, no deformation at contact. BOTTOM ROW same colored same-shaped SOFT alternatives pressed by SAME adult index finger in SAME pose, obvious broad compression/indentation beneath finger. Finger present in BOTH rows and all cells, never covers object. Col1 yellow painted wooden cube vs yellow sponge cube compressed; col2 blue rigid plastic ball vs blue squeezable foam ball compressed; col3 smooth gray stone vs gray soft modeling-clay rounded lump with deep finger indentation; col4 red rigid wooden rectangular block vs red cushion/foam rectangular block compressed; col5 purple rigid plastic cylinder vs purple squeezable foam cylinder compressed. Complete hand finger contact plus object fits well inside tile safe margins, no extra fingers/duplicated anatomy. HARD objects keep rigid outline. SOFT clear deformation but not broken or dirty. Do NOT imply hard=heavy or soft=small, keep paired scales.
